subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@finlex.com>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha@finlex.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Sam / Asha —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned on next steps and success criteria. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Pain points and drivers
- Cost volatility and token pricing on current proprietary APIs (OpenAI + Anthropic).
- Need for deterministic cost model for high-volume legal document generation and embeddings.
- Data residency and auditability requirements for regulatory reviews (logs + KMS integration).
- Latency spikes during peak ingest and batch generation jobs affecting downstream workflows.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Frontend call flow -> backend service that calls OpenAI Chat Completions + Anthropic for safety checks.
- Post-processing pipeline in GCP (BigQuery + Pub/Sub) for embeddings and indexing.
- Vault-based key management, SSO via Okta.

Success criteria for migration
1) Match or improve latency p95 for < 350ms per request for short-form responses and < 800ms for larger doc summaries.
2) Reduce per-document inference cost by 40% (target).
3) Keep QA/regulatory observability: full audit logs + customer-managed KMS.
4) Compatibility with current prompt/tooling (fewest changes to prompt shape and function calling).

Model / compatibility needs
- Need support for chat-style completions and embeddings; function/tool-calling support is nice-to-have.
- Prefer Open weights / FOSS-compatible models or permissive licenses.
- Quantized model variants desirable for cost.

Next steps (owners + timeline)
- I’ll put together a short compatibility matrix and a model shortlist that maps to your latency/cost targets (Marissa) — by end of day Tuesday.
- You’ll share the completed security questionnaire and any procurement timelines (Sam / Asha).
- Follow-up technical deep-dive and Ops sync to validate KV-cache and batching strategy (Rishi + Aditya) — target week of 10/26.

Attachments: I’ll include a security pack and an initial SOW draft in the next email.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks for the clear recap and the plan. This matches our internal notes. A few clarifications:

- Latency: the p95 numbers you listed are what we’d need in production. We have a few batch jobs that tolerate higher latency but the interactive summarization must meet p95 targets.
- Cost: the 40% reduction is aspirational but required for our CFO sign-off; happy to see the model shortlist.
- Security: we will need HSM/KMS integration and SOC2 evidence; I attached our procurement security questionnaire for your team to fill.

Thanks Sam — attaching the items now and answering your question below.

Quick answers to compatibility questions
- API compatibility: Redwood provides a REST API with a compatibility layer for common OpenAI/Anthropic request shapes (chat + embeddings). In practice customers can often switch with small adapter code; we’ll include example adapters for Node/Python.
- Function calling: we support structured function-like calls via our API and can map common OpenAI function call patterns.
- Embeddings: supported as a first-class endpoint, with options to return vectors or index-ready payloads.

Model shortlist (initial) mapped to your targets
- Llama 3 (quantized variants) — strong for chat, good community support; latency medium; licensing OK for many customers.
- Mistral Instruct (7B/8B quantized) — lower latency, good cost profile for embeddings + generation.
- RedPine-xx (Redwood-verified opt variant) — higher throughput on our runtime; still verifying instruction tuning fidelity.
- OpenEmbed family (for embeddings) — high quality vectors at lower compute.

Attachments in this email:
- Redwood_Security_Pack_v2.pdf (SOC2 overview, audit contacts, KMS integrations)
- SOW_FinLex_v0.1.docx (initial scope + assumptions)
- Model_Compatibility_Matrix.csv (row per model, columns: chat_compatibility, embedding_quality, quantization_support, expected_p95_ms)

Next steps
- I’ll fill the security questionnaire and return it by EOD tomorrow (Marissa).
- Rishi and Aditya will schedule the ops deep-dive to validate batching/KV-cache approach (target week of 10/26).

If that looks right I’ll send a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive and attach the filled questionnaire.

Best,
